Metals and nonmetals:
Elements are divided into metals, nonmetals and metalloids. Metals are shiny, malleable, ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity. Most are solid at room temperature (mercury is liquid) and have high density and melting point.

Nonmetals are usually dull, brittle and poor conductors, and they can be solids, liquids or gases. Graphite is a nonmetal that conducts electricity. Metalloids such as silicon have mixed properties.

The use of a material depends on its properties: copper for wires, aluminum for light objects. An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, such as steel. Density = mass ÷ volume.
Reactivity of metals:
Reactivity is how easily a metal reacts. The reactivity series from most to least reactive is potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminum, zinc, iron, lead, (hydrogen), copper, silver, gold.

Reactive metals form oxides with oxygen, and those above hydrogen react with dilute acids to give hydrogen gas. Sodium and potassium react quickly with cold water: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2.

A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu. Unreactive metals such as gold are found pure in nature. Other metals are found in ores.
Atomic structure and electron arrangemen:
An atom has a nucleus with protons (+1) and neutrons (0), and electrons (-1) in shells around it. Atomic number Z is the number of protons. Mass number A = protons + neutrons. In a neutral atom, electrons = protons.

Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. Electrons fill shells from the nucleus outward. For the first 20 elements the shells hold 2, 8, 8, 2 electrons in order.

The electrons in the outer shell are valence electrons, and they decide chemical behavior. A full outer shell makes an atom stable. Losing or gaining electrons forms ions.
The periodic table:
The periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number. Rows are periods (7) and columns are groups (18). The period number equals the number of electron shells in use.

Elements in the same group have similar properties because they have the same number of valence electrons. Group 1 has 1, group 2 has 2, and groups 13 to 18 have 3 to 8.

Group 1 are alkali metals, group 17 are halogens, and group 18 are noble gases, which are unreactive. Metals are on the left and in the middle, nonmetals on the right, and metalloids along the zigzag line between them. Mendeleev predicted undiscovered elements from gaps in his table.
Useful elements: nitrogen, phosphorus, s:
Nitrogen is 78% of air as unreactive N2. It is used to make ammonia (N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3) and fertilizers. Phosphorus is needed for DNA, bones and fertilizers, and it is used in matches.

Sulfur is a yellow solid used to make sulfuric acid and to harden rubber. Burning sulfur compounds makes SO2, which causes acid rain.

Chlorine (Cl2) is a poisonous yellow-green gas that kills germs in water and is used to make bleach and PVC. Fluorine is the most reactive nonmetal, and fluoride in toothpaste protects teeth. Percentage of an element = element mass in formula ÷ molar mass × 100.
Natural and synthetic polymers:
A polymer is a long molecule made of many repeating small units called monomers. Joining monomers is polymerization.

Natural polymers are made by living things: starch and cellulose (from glucose), proteins (from amino acids), DNA and natural rubber. Synthetic polymers are made in industry, mostly from crude oil: polyethylene (from ethene, C2H4), PVC, polystyrene, nylon, PET and Teflon.

Polymers are usually light, flexible and waterproof. Many synthetic polymers do not decay easily, so reducing, reusing and recycling plastic is important.
